Ghost cards that a `werk build` / `werk run` proposes describe code in the target repository (`node src/cli.ts target`, on 2026-10-24 `/Users/eryk.napierala/Projects/werk-v0`: main plus `werk-build/*` branches), not the werk prototype in the worktree.

**Why:** in the 2026-10-23 review of 28 pipeline proposals, the first code checks read the prototype's `src/`. That gave false "mismatch" and "contradiction" verdicts on about 8 cards, and every one changed after a recheck in werk-v0.

**How to apply:** before you fact-check a pipeline proposal, or brief a reviewer to do it, run `node src/cli.ts target` and check that repo first. Name the repo in the finding. Many reviewers that write to the log at the same time need a lock, because the log append has none (see [[reproposal-revives-old-edges]]).

`werk rework` reports the rework per ticket: cited cards reopened and merged code changed
why: Code rework is read from the repository, and one report over every merge takes tens of seconds. A command run on demand keeps that cost out of every read of the measures.

```
werk rework [--json]
```

- It reads the board log, the decision log and the target repository, and writes nothing (#ms-outcome-rework).
- For each ticket with rework it prints one row: the cited cards reopened after its build started, and the lines its merge added that a later commit changed within the window.
- It prints the totals, the merges whose window is still open, and the merges whose commits the repository no longer holds.
- `--json` prints the same report as one JSON object.

card ms-outcome-rework  [decided]
Rework: decided cards reopened and merged code changed soon after a build
why: Work that is undone soon after it is done costs twice. Rework shows it even when no one filed a follow-up. Both kinds are folds over records that exist already: the reopen events of the decision log, the cited cards of each ticket, and the merge commit of each ticket.

Two kinds:

- **A cited card reopened.** A decided card is reopened after a ticket that cites it started to build. The reopen events come from the decision log (#pr-log), and the cards a ticket cites, with the time it cited them, from the ticket's cite records (#st-ticket-watch).
- **Merged code changed.** A later commit changes or reverts a line that a ticket's merge added, within 14 days of that merge. The fold reads the merge commit that the board log records for each ticket (#st-build-run), and asks the repository at the time of the report. Nothing new is recorded at merge time.

**Numbers.** Rework events per ticket, by kind. The 14 days are a first guess.

Example. Ticket app/01 cites #app-login and merges on 1 May as commit 9f2c.

1. 3 May — #app-login is reopened. Rework: a cited card reopened.
2. 6 May — a commit rewrites two lines that 9f2c added. Rework: merged code changed.
3. 20 May — another commit changes a line that 9f2c added. That is past 14 days, so it is not rework.

```
1 May merge 9f2c ─┬─ 3 May reopen #app-login   ── rework (card)
                  ├─ 6 May commit edits 9f2c   ── rework (code)
                  └─ 20 May commit edits 9f2c  ── past 14 days, not counted
```

  -> refines         ms-outcome  The pipeline measures what it gets wrong and where it needs a person
  -> depends_on      pr-log  The map is stored as an append-only event log, and the cards are folded from it
       why: Card reopens are read from the reopen events of the append-only decision log that this card defines.
  -> depends_on      st-ticket-watch  A change to a cited card blocks every open ticket that cites it
       why: The cards each ticket cites, and when, come from the cite records that this card defines.
  -> depends_on      st-build-run  The merge loop: queue one ticket, merge it, then run the held-out set
       why: The merge commit of each ticket, which the code fold starts from, is recorded by the merge loop that this card defines.
  <- alternative_to  ms-outcome-rework:opt0  Record the lines each merge adds, and watch them for changes
  <- depends_on      werk-cli-rework  `werk rework` reports the rework per ticket: cited cards reopened and merged code changed
Options
